briefing.summary: Survey Monterey Canyon's north wall, then follow the upper channel toward Moss Landing. Visit the shallow canyon head or the MARS seafloor observatory node for optional scans.
facts: Monterey Canyon begins right off the beach at Moss Landing -- so close to shore that MBARI, headquartered there, calls it their 'backyard'.

MBARI traces the main channel more than 470 km offshore, through the Monterey Deep Sea Fan to depths beyond 4,000 m; the walls reach about 1,700 m high. This tile covers only the upper part, to about 2,333 m.
Between the head marker and the next scan point, this terrain grid drops from about 44 m to 265 m over about 2.85 km in a straight line.

Turbidity currents -- fast underwater avalanches of sediment -- have been measured moving down this canyon at up to about 7 m/s, some travelling more than 50 km. They happen several times a year in the upper canyon.
The MBARI-operated MARS observatory node, on the continental slope at 891 m, is a real cabled power-and-data outlet for deep-sea science instruments, connected to shore by a 52 km cable.
hazards: Turbidity currents: sudden, fast-moving sediment flows can occur without warning, especially in the upper canyon.
Strong currents, including internal tidal flows along the canyon.
Fishing gear may be present, especially in shallower water near the head.
Sunlight fades with depth; use your lights to read the deeper terrain.

objectives.title: Survey the north canyon wall
objectives.hint: Face the nearby north wall, around 750 m.

objectives.title: Follow the upper channel
objectives.hint: Follow the channel east toward Moss Landing, rising to around 265 m.

objectives.title: Scan the canyon head
objectives.hint: Continue east to the shallow canyon head off Moss Landing, around 45 m.

objectives.title: Find the MARS observatory node
objectives.hint: Travel far west from the canyon head to the MARS node, near 890 m.
